primitives.name: Multi-Class Object Detection
primitives.verbatim_quote: This project develops an end-to-end system that combines a YOLO object detector with the ByteTrack tracking algorithm to identify and track players, referees, goalkeepers, and the ball throughout a match.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'D': 'Detection confidence score (dimensionless)', 'B': 'Bounding box coordinates (pixels)', 'T': 'Temporal frame index (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Objects are static or slowly moving within a single frame; camera motion is negligible.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Ball detection fails under occlusion or low-light conditions.

layer2.mapping: Detection function D(B,T) maps pixel-space bounding boxes to semantic classes via trained YOLOv8s classifier.
layer2.telemetry: mAP50 score for class-wise detection accuracy.

primitives.name: ByteTrack Multi-Object Tracking
primitives.verbatim_quote: This project develops an end-to-end system that combines a YOLO object detector with the ByteTrack tracking algorithm to identify and track players, referees, goalkeepers, and the ball throughout a match.
primitives.assumptions: Identity persistence across frames; minimal inter-object overlap.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Tracking fails during severe occlusion or rapid motion.

layer2.mapping: ByteTrack kernel K(I,P,V) maintains object identity over time by associating detections with existing tracks based on IoU and appearance features.
layer2.telemetry: ID switch rate and mean average precision (mAP) for tracking consistency.

primitives.name: Broadcast Footage Ingestion
primitives.verbatim_quote: Specifically, this study answers the question: Can Artificial Intelligence be used to reliably detect and track soccer players, goalkeepers, balls, and referees using a single broadcast camera?
primitives.assumptions: Video stream is temporally synchronized; frame sampling preserves motion continuity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Ingestion fails at high frame rates without sufficient computational bandwidth.

layer2.mapping: Input pipeline I(F,S,C) transforms raw broadcast video into a sequence of sampled frames for downstream processing.
layer2.telemetry: Frame drop rate and latency between ingestion and processing.

The core methodology integrates YOLOv8s for detection and ByteTrack for tracking, forming a dual-stage pipeline. Detection operates in pixel space with bounding box regression, while tracking maintains object identities through temporal association. The system assumes stable camera conditions and minimal occlusion. Failures occur when ball occlusion disrupts tracking or when lighting degrades detection quality. The framework's scalability stems from its reliance on standard broadcast footage, eliminating hardware dependency. Mathematical duality exists between detection (spatial localization) and tracking (temporal identity maintenance), which together form a coherent state-space representation of the soccer field. The system's robustness hinges on feature extraction fidelity and temporal coherence in object motion estimation.
